q: (Allaah's punishment is so close to the Kuffaar that it may be said that it)
has arrived, so do not try to hurry it
(by constantly asking when it will come).
is Pure and Exalted above what
(none can therefore be equal to Him).
v.s: The command of God is coming, so be not impatient for it. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
v.c: The command of Allah is at hand, so do not hasten it. Glorified and Exalted is He above what they associate ˹with Him in worship˺!

q: sends the angels with revelation to those bondsmen of His whom He desires
v.s: He sends down the angels, with the inspiration [i.e., revelation] of His command, upon whom He wills of His servants, [telling them], "Warn that there is no deity except Me; so fear Me."
v.c: He sends down the angels with revelation by His command to whoever He wills of His servants, ˹stating:˺ “Warn ˹humanity˺ that there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Me, so be mindful of Me ˹alone˺.”

q: (A logical proof for this belief that only Allaah deserves to be worshipped is that)
He created the heavens and the earth with truth
He is Exalted above the partners that they
v.s: He created the heavens and earth in truth. High is He above what they associate with Him.
v.c: He created the heavens and the earth for a purpose. Exalted is He above what they associate with Him ˹in worship˺!

q: He created man from a drop of fluid
(and then developed him into an adult)
man is suddenly an open enemy
(who contests the fact that Allaah can resurrect him on the Day of Qiyaamah).
v.s: He created man from a sperm-drop; then at once he is a clear adversary.
v.c: He created humans from a sperm-drop, then—behold!—they openly challenge ˹Him˺.

q: also created livestock. In them is warmth for you
(when you use their skins for clothing),
v.s: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat.
v.c: And He created the cattle for you as a source of warmth, food, and ˹many other˺ benefits.

q: for you when you return them
in the evenings and when you send them out
(the owner of livestock is pleased when he sees his animals proceed to and from the pastures, producing and reproducing profitably).
v.s: And for you in them is [the enjoyment of] beauty when you bring them in [for the evening] and when you send them out [to pasture].
v.c: They are also pleasing to you when you bring them home and when you take them out to graze.

q: to such destinations that you could not reach
without great difficulty to yourselves. Without doubt your Rabb is the Most Pardoning, Most Merciful
v.s: And they carry your loads to a land you could not have reached except with difficulty to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.
v.c: And they carry your loads to ˹distant˺ lands which you could not otherwise reach without great hardship. Surely your Lord is Ever Gracious, Most Merciful.

q: Horses, mules and donkeys for riding and adornment. And
He creates such things about which you have no knowledge
(such as modern means of transport which the people of earlier times did not know).
v.s: And [He created] the horses, mules and donkeys for you to ride and [as] adornment. And He creates that which you do not know.
v.c: ˹He also created˺ horses, mules, and donkeys for your transportation and adornment. And He creates what you do not know.

m: surely He would have guided you
q: who deviate from it. If He wills He could guide
(However, He does not will this for reasons He knows best).
v.s: And upon God is the direction of the [right] way, and among them [i.e., the various paths] are those deviating. And if He willed, He could have guided you all.
v.c: It is upon Allah ˹alone˺ to ˹clearly˺ show the Straight Way. Other ways are deviant. Had He willed, He would have easily imposed guidance upon all of you.

q: Allaah is the One Who sends rain for you from the sky, which provides
water and vegetation on which you graze your animals.
v.s: It is He who sends down rain from the sky; from it is drink and from it is foliage in which you pasture [animals].
v.c: He is the One Who sends down rain from the sky, from which you drink and by which plants grow for your cattle to graze.

q: Allaah grows for you plantations, olives, dates, grapes and all types of fruit. Undoubtedly there is an Aayah
in this for those who reflect
v.s: He causes to grow for you thereby the crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and from all the fruits. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
v.c: With it He produces for you ˹various˺ crops, olives, palm trees, grapevines, and every type of fruit. Surely in this is a sign for those who reflect.

q: He placed the night and the day at your service
(so that you may use each of them for your benefit),
and the sun and the moon as well
(each of which benefit mankind to a great extent).
The stars are also kept in servitude by His command. Indeed there are Aayaat in this for people of understanding.
v.s: And He has subjected for you the night and day and the sun and moon, and the stars are subjected by His command. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason.
v.c: And He has subjected for your benefit the day and the night, the sun and the moon. And the stars have been subjected by His command. Surely in this are signs for those who understand.

q: the things that He has created for you on the earth, having various colours
Surely there is an Aayah in this for people who take heed.
v.s: And [He has subjected] whatever He multiplied for you on the earth of varying colors. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who remember.
v.c: And ˹He subjected˺ for you whatever He has created on earth of varying colours. Surely in this is a sign for those who are mindful.

q: It is He Who subjugated the ocean
so that you may eat fresh meat
You see the ships cleaving their way on it
from His bounty and so that you may show gratitude to Him
v.s: And it is He who subjected the sea for you to eat from it tender meat and to extract from it ornaments which you wear. And you see the ships plowing through it, and [He subjected it] that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
v.c: And He is the One Who has subjected the sea, so from it you may eat tender seafood and extract ornaments to wear. And you see the ships ploughing their way through it, so you may seek His bounty and give thanks ˹to Him˺.

q: mountains on the earth so that it
does not shake with you and
on earth so that you may find your way
v.s: And He has cast into the earth firmly set mountains, lest it shift with you, and [made] rivers and roads, that you may be guided,
v.c: He has placed into the earth firm mountains, so it does not shake with you, as well as rivers, and pathways so you may find your way.

q: (such as mountains, trees and other clearly distinguishable land features by which man can find his way and recognise his location. Without them, every place will look the same)
(at sea where there are no marks and during the night when they are not visible)
v.s: And landmarks. And by the stars they are [also] guided.
v.c: Also by landmarks and stars do people find their way.

q: Is he who cannot create like Him Who can create?
(It is obvious that the gods of the Kuffaar who cannot create anything can never be compared to Allaah Who has created everything. After understanding this,)
v.s: Then is He who creates like one who does not create? So will you not be reminded?
v.c: Can the One Who creates be equal to those who do not? Will you not then be mindful?

q: Allaah's bounties, you will never be able to do so
Verily Allaah is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful.
v.s: And if you should count the favors of God, you could not enumerate them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
v.c: If you tried to count Allah’s blessings, you would never be able to number them. Surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

q: (No person should think that he can escape answering to Allaah for his actions because)
secret) and what you make public.
v.s: And God knows what you conceal and what you declare.
v.c: And Allah knows what you conceal and what you reveal.

q: (by Allaah. It is therefore Allaah Who deserves to be worshipped and not anyone else).
v.s: And those they invoke other than God create nothing, and they [themselves] are created.
v.c: But those ˹idols˺ they invoke besides Allah cannot create anything—they themselves are created.

q: (Even if the Mushrikeen worship living creatures, these gods have been created by Allaah and)
They do not even know when they will be raised
(they have no knowledge of the unseen and therefore can not be equal to Allaah at all).
v.s: They are [in fact] dead, not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected.
v.c: They are dead, not alive—not even knowing when their followers will be resurrected.

q: Your Ilaah is but One Ilaah
(none can match His attributes and cannot be equal to Him). (However,)
The hearts of those who disbelieve in the Aakhirah are
(too proud to accept that they have to worship Allaah).
v.s: Your god is one God. But those who do not believe in the Hereafter - their hearts are disapproving, and they are arrogant.
v.c: Your God is ˹only˺ One God. As for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, their hearts are in denial, and they are too proud.

q: (Such people will never be able to escape from Allaah because)
Without any doubt Allaah knows what they keep
secret and what they make public. Indeed He does not love the proud ones
(and will punish them for their pride).
v.s: Assuredly, God knows what they conceal and what they declare. Indeed, He does not like the arrogant.
v.c: Without a doubt, Allah knows what they conceal and what they reveal. He certainly does not like those who are too proud.

q: (by people wanting to know about Islaam),
they reply, “Tales of the ancient people.”
(Although the Mushrikeen of Makkah knew that the Qur'aan must be from Allaah, they made statements like this to discourage others from drawing close) to Islaam.)
v.s: And when it is said to them, "What has your Lord sent down?" they say, "Legends of the former peoples,"
v.c: And when it is said to them, “What has your Lord revealed?” They say, “Ancient fables!”

q: That they will carry their entire burdens
on the Day of Qiyaamah together with some of the burdens
(they will be held responsible for the wrongs that they led others to carry out, just as those people will also be punished for their sins).
Evil indeed is the burden that they bear
(because it will land them in jahannam).
v.s: That they may bear their own burdens [i.e., sins] in full on the Day of Resurrection and some of the burdens of those whom they misguide without [i.e., by lack of] knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.
v.c: Let them bear their burdens in full on the Day of Judgment as well as some of the burdens of those they mislead without knowledge. Evil indeed is what they will bear!

q: from the foundation, causing the roof to
cave in on them from above
punishment came to them from a source they did not perceive
v.s: Those before them had already plotted, but God came at [i.e., uprooted] their building from the foundations, so the roof fell upon them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.
v.c: Indeed, those before them had plotted, but Allah struck at the ˹very˺ foundation of their structure, so the roof collapsed on top of them, and the torment came upon them from where they did not expect.

q: Then He shall humiliate them on the Day of Qiyaamah and ask, “Where are those partners of Mine
that you used to argue about
(with the Mu'mineen with such force)?” (They will have no answer to give because their gods will be unable to assist them. Seeing this predicament of the Kaafiroon,)
will say, “Today humiliation and misfortune are certainly the lot of the Kaafiroon!”
v.s: Then on the Day of Resurrection He will disgrace them and say, "Where are My 'partners' for whom you used to oppose [the believers]?" Those who were given knowledge will say, "Indeed disgrace, this Day, and evil are upon the disbelievers" -
v.c: Then on the Day of Judgment He will humiliate them and say, “Where are My ˹so-called˺ associate-gods for whose sake you used to oppose ˹the believers˺?” Those gifted with knowledge will say, “Surely disgrace and misery today are upon the disbelievers.”

q: Those whose souls were claimed by the angels while they oppressed themselves
(kufr and Shirk)!” (The angels of death replied,)
Allaah is well aware of what you used to do
(He knows the evil you carried out and will punish you for it).'
v.s: The ones whom the angels take in death [while] wronging themselves, and [who] then offer submission, [saying], "We were not doing any evil." But, yes! Indeed, God is Knowing of what you used to do.
v.c: Those whose souls the angels seize while they wrong themselves will then offer ˹full˺ submission ˹and say falsely,˺ “We did not do any evil.” ˹The angels will say,˺ “No! Surely Allah fully knows what you used to do.

q: (They will therefore be told on the Day of Qiyaamah,)
“Enter the doors of Jahannam to live there forever. Evil indeed is the abode of the proud ones
(those who were too proud to accept Imaan)!”
v.s: So enter the gates of Hell to abide eternally therein, and how wretched is the residence of the arrogant.
v.c: So enter the gates of Hell, to stay there forever. Indeed, what an evil home for the arrogant!”

q: are asked, “What has your Rabb revealed
(very differently from the Mushrikeen and say), “(Our Rabb has revealed)
for those who did good in this world and the home of the Aakhirah
How grand is the home of those who have Taqwa
v.s: And it will be said to those who feared God, "What did your Lord send down?" They will say, "[That which is] good." For those who do good in this world is good; and the home of the Hereafter is better. And how excellent is the home of the righteous -
v.c: And ˹when˺ it is said to those mindful ˹of Allah˺, “What has your Lord revealed?” They say, “All the best!” For those who do good in this world, there is goodness. But far better is the ˹eternal˺ Home of the Hereafter. How excellent indeed is the home of the righteous:

q: They will enter Jannaat of eternity beneath which rivers flow. There they shall have whatever they desire
In this manner does Allaah reward those who adopt Taqwa.
v.s: Gardens of perpetual residence, which they will enter, beneath which rivers flow. They will have therein whatever they wish. Thus does God reward the righteous -
v.c: the Gardens of Eternity which they will enter, under which rivers flow. In it they will have whatever they desire. This is how Allah rewards the righteous—

q: Those whose souls the angels claim while they are pure. They
(to them on the Day of Qiyaamah),
“Peace be upon you. Enter Jannah because of the
v.s: The ones whom the angels take in death, [being] good and pure; [the angels] will say, "Peace be upon you. Enter Paradise for what you used to do."
v.c: those whose souls the angels take while they are virtuous, saying ˹to them˺, “Peace be upon you! Enter Paradise for what you used to do.”

q: Are they (the Kuffaar) waiting for the angels
to come to them or for the order
Those before them behaved in the same way
(they also refused to accept Imaan until it was too late).
(because He had sent the Ambiyaa ﵊ to convey the message of Imaan to them)
v.s: Do they [i.e., the disbelievers] await [anything] except that the angels should come to them or there comes the command of your Lord? Thus did those do before them. And God wronged them not, but they had been wronging themselves.
v.c: Are they only awaiting the coming of the angels or the command of your Lord ˹O Prophet˺? So were those before them. And Allah never wronged them, but it was they who wronged themselves.

q: So they received the punishment of their evil acts and
v.s: So they were struck by the evil consequences of what they did and were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
v.c: Then the evil ˹consequences˺ of their deeds overtook them, and they were overwhelmed by what they used to ridicule.

q: Those who commit Shirk say, “If Allaah willed, then neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything besides Him, and we would never have forbidden anything
(without His command. They failed to realise that Allaah does not force people to do anything, but gives them a choice).
Those before them behaved in the same manner
(They also said the same things and rejected their Rusul). (However, it is not the duty of the Rusul to force people to accept Imaan because)
The responsibility of the Rusul is only clear propagation
(after which people have the choice to either accept Imaan or not to accept).
v.s: And those who associate others with God say, "If God had willed, we would not have worshipped anything other than Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything through other than Him." Thus did those do before them. So is there upon the messengers except [the duty of] clear notification?
v.c: The polytheists argue, “Had Allah willed, neither we nor our forefathers would have worshipped anything other than Him, nor prohibited anything without His command.” So did those before them. Is not the messengers’ duty only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly?

q: Indeed We have sent a Rasool among every nation
to “Worship Allaah and shun the Shaytaan
(idols and false gods).” (From among the people to whom the Rusul came,)
There were those of them whom Allaah had guided and those for whom deviation had been decreed
(who were destined to die as Kuffaar).
So travel in the land and see what was the
v.s: And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], “Worship God and avoid tāghūt.” And among them were those whom God guided, and among them were those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed. So proceed [i.e., travel] through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers.
v.c: We surely sent a messenger to every community, saying, “Worship Allah and shun false gods.” But some of them were guided by Allah, while others were destined to stray. So travel throughout the land and see the fate of the deniers!

q: (there is nothing you can do about it if Allaah does not guide them because)
Allaah surely does not guide those whom He has sent astray
(who have been destined to die as Kuffaar),
and they shall have no helpers
v.s: [Even] if you should strive for their guidance, [O Muhammad], indeed, God does not guide those He sends astray, and they will have no helpers.
v.c: Even though you ˹O Prophet˺ are keen on their guidance, Allah certainly does not guide those He leaves to stray, and they will have no helpers.

q: swear their most solemn oaths by Allaah that Allaah will never resurrect the dead. No
is indeed a resolute promise that Allaah has made, but most people do not know.
v.s: And they swear by God their strongest oaths [that] God will not resurrect one who dies. But yes - [it is] a true promise [binding] upon Him, but most of the people do not know.
v.c: They swear by Allah their most solemn oaths that Allah will never raise the dead to life. Yes ˹He will˺! It is a true promise binding on Him, but most people do not know.

q: So that Allaah may make clear to them
the matters in which they differed
and so that the Kuffaar may come to know that they were liars
(in their statements when they rejected the message of the Ambiyaa),
v.s: [It is] so He will make clear to them [the truth of] that wherein they differ and so those who have disbelieved may know that they were liars.
v.c: ˹He will do that˺ to make clear to them what they disagreed on, and for the disbelievers to know that they were liars.

q: (Resurrection and all other matters are extremely simple for Us because)
When We intend anything, all We have to do is say, “Be!” and it becomes
(whatever We had intended it to be).
v.s: Indeed, Our word to a thing when We intend it is but that We say to it, "Be," and it is.
v.c: If We ever will something ˹to exist˺, all We say is: “Be!” And it is!

m: surely We will give them position
q: As for those who make Hijrah for
Allaah after being oppressed, We shall certainly settle them in a pleasant abode on earth.
is greater, if only they knew
(if people knew the rewards for making Hijrah, none would hesitate to do so).
v.s: And those who emigrated for [the cause of] God after they had been wronged - We will surely settle them in this world in a good place; but the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if only they could know.
v.c: As for those who emigrated in ˹the cause of˺ Allah after being persecuted, We will surely bless them with a good home in this world. But the reward of the Hereafter is far better, if only they knew.

q: (to see to their well-being and to the well-being of their families). (When people rely on Allaah, He provides for them from sources they least expect.)
v.s: [They are] those who endured patiently and upon their Lord relied.
v.c: ˹It is˺ they who have patiently endured, and in their Lord they put their trust.

q: as Ambiyaa, sending revelation to them. So
(those who understood the Torah and Injeel as they were revealed)
(that a Nabi sent to mankind has to be a man).
v.s: And We sent not before you except men to whom We revealed [Our message]. So ask the people of the message [i.e., former scriptures] if you do not know.
v.c: We did not send ˹messengers˺ before you ˹O Prophet˺ except mere men inspired by Us. If you ˹polytheists˺ do not know ˹this already˺, then ask those who have knowledge ˹of the Scriptures˺.

q: books. We have revealed the Reminder
has been revealed to them, and so that they may reflect
v.s: [We sent them] with clear proofs and written ordinances. And We revealed to you the message [i.e., the Qur’ān] that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them and that they might give thought.
v.c: ˹We sent them˺ with clear proofs and divine Books. And We have sent down to you ˹O Prophet˺ the Reminder, so that you may explain to people what has been revealed for them, and perhaps they will reflect.

q: Do those who plot evil schemes
assured that Allaah will not plunge them into the earth or afflict them with a punishment from a source they do not perceive?
v.s: Then, do those who have planned evil deeds feel secure that God will not cause the earth to swallow them or that the punishment will not come upon them from where they do not perceive?
v.c: Do those who devise evil plots feel secure that Allah will not cause the earth to swallow them? Or that the torment will not come upon them in ways they cannot comprehend?

q: that He will not seize them
activities, after which they will have no escape?
v.s: Or that He would not seize them during their [usual] activity, and they could not cause failure [i.e., escape from Him]?
v.c: Or that He will not seize them while they go about ˹their day˺, for then they will have no escape?

q: that He will not seize them with a gradual depletion
(causing their condition to deteriorate gradually until there is nothing left of them)?
Without doubt your Rabb is Most Pardoning, Most Merciful
(He does not punish people immediately, but allows them time to repent).
v.s: Or that He would not seize them gradually [in a state of dread]? But indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful.
v.c: Or that He will not destroy them gradually? But your Lord is truly Ever Gracious, Most Merciful.

q: Do they not see the things that Allaah has created, the shadows of which sway to the right and the left
(as the sun moves across the sky),
v.s: Have they not considered what things God has created? Their shadows incline to the right and to the left, prostrating to God, while they [i.e., those creations] are humble.
v.c: Have they not considered how the shadows of everything Allah has created incline to the right and the left ˹as the sun moves˺, totally submitting to Allah in all humility?

q: To Allaah's command, all within the heavens and the earth prostrate
including all creatures and angels, and they are not proud
(they do not consider it below their dignity to submit to Allaah. In fact, they regard it as an honour).
v.s: And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels [as well], and they are not arrogant.
v.c: And to Allah ˹alone˺ bows down ˹in submission˺ whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of living creatures, as do the angels—who are not too proud ˹to do so˺.

q: fear the authority of their Rabb and do
(One who recites or hears this verse being recited should perform Sajdah.)
v.s: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
v.c: They fear their Lord above them, and do whatever they are commanded.

q: two deities. He is but One Ilaah, so fear Me only.”
v.s: And God has said, "Do not take for yourselves two deities. He [i.e., God] is but one God, so fear only Me."
v.c: And Allah has said, “Do not take two gods. There is only One God. So be in awe of Me ˹alone˺.”

q: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth and obedience is always for Him
(only He should be obeyed at all times).
Do you fear any other besides Allaah?
v.s: And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is [due] worship constantly. Then is it other than God that you fear?
v.c: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him ˹alone˺ is the everlasting devotion. Will you then fear any other than Allah?

q: Every bounty that you possess is from Allaah. Thereafter,
when any difficulty afflicts you, you must appeal only to Him
(to assist you. You must do this because you know that no one else will be able to assist you).
v.s: And whatever you have of favor - it is from God. Then when adversity touches you, to Him you cry for help.
v.c: Whatever blessings you have are from Allah. Then whenever hardship touches you, to Him ˹alone˺ you cry ˹for help˺.

q: When He removes the difficulty from you, suddenly
a group from you ascribes partners to their Rabb...
v.s: Then when He removes the adversity from you, at once a party of you associates others with their Lord
v.c: Then as soon as He removes the hardship from you, a group of you associates ˹others˺ with their Lord ˹in worship˺,

q: ...so as to reject the favours granted to them
(Although they prayed to Allaah when in difficulty, as soon as they were saved, they ignored His favour of saving them and continued praying to their other gods, as if they had assisted them).
Enjoy yourselves. Soon you will come to learn
(the error of your ways when Allaah's punishment strikes).
v.s: So they will deny what We have given them. Then enjoy yourselves, for you are going to know.
v.c: only returning Our favours with ingratitude. So enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know.

q: set aside a portion of what
We provide for them to those

(As mentioned in verse 136 of Surah 6, where Allaah says, “A portion of their crops and animals that Allaah created, they set aside for Allaah saying, “This is for Allaah,” according to their estimation, “and this is for our partners.”)
v.s: And they assign to what they do not know [i.e., false deities] a portion of that which We have provided them. By God, you will surely be questioned about what you used to invent.
v.c: And they ˹even˺ assign to those ˹idols˺—who know nothing—a share of what We have provided for them. By Allah! You will certainly be questioned about whatever ˹lies˺ you used to fabricate ˹against Allah˺.

q: (by saying that the angels are Allaah's daughters).
have for themselves what they desire
(sons). (Allaah highlights the selfishness of the Mushrikeen who loved to have sons for themselves, yet they ascribe daughters to Allaah.)
v.s: And they attribute to God daughters - exalted is He - and for them is what they desire [i.e., sons].
v.c: And they attribute ˹angels as˺ daughters to Allah—glory be to Him!— the opposite of what they desire for themselves.

q: (Describing the dislike that the Mushrikeen had for daughters during the Period of Ignorance, Allaah says,)
When any of them is given the good news of a daughter
v.s: And when one of them is informed of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief.
v.c: Whenever one of them is given the good news of a baby girl, his face grows gloomy, as he suppresses his rage.

m: he has been given good news
q: He hides from the people because of the terrible news that he received
(he is ashamed to face others because they will ridicule him). (He then asks himself)
Must he keep her with disgrace or bury her in the sand? Evil indeed is the decision that they
(when they decide to attribute daughters to Allaah whereas they themselves have such a great dislike for daughters)!
v.s: He hides himself from the people because of the ill of which he has been informed. Should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the ground? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide.
v.c: He hides himself from the people because of the bad news he has received. Should he keep her in disgrace, or bury her ˹alive˺ in the ground? Evil indeed is their judgment!

q: who are not convinced of the Aakhirah
(because they dislike daughters, whom the entire society needs),
while Allaah's are the most sublime attributes
and He is the Mighty, the Wise.
v.s: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is the description [i.e., an attribute] of evil; and for God is the highest attribute. And He is Exalted in Might, the Wise.
v.c: To those who disbelieve in the Hereafter belong all evil qualities, whereas to Allah belong the finest attributes. And He is the Almighty, All-Wise.

q: If Allaah were to take people to task for their injustice
He would not have left a single creature
(because the punishment affecting the people would have also killed everything else),
When their term expires, they will not be able to delay it for a moment, nor bring it forward.
v.s: And if God were to impose blame on the people for their wrongdoing, He would not have left upon it [i.e., the earth] any creature, but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].
v.c: If Allah were to punish people ˹immediately˺ for their wrongdoing, He would not have left a single living being on earth. But He delays them for an appointed term. And when their time arrives, they cannot delay it for a moment, nor could they advance it.

q: They assign to Allaah what they dislike
make the false claims that they shall receive goodness
Without doubt they shall have the Fire
(of Jahannam and not Jannah in the Aakhirah),
and they will be the first to be condemned
v.s: And they attribute to God that which they dislike [i.e., daughters], and their tongues assert the lie that they will have the best [from Him]. Assuredly, they will have the Fire, and they will be [therein] neglected.
v.c: They attribute to Allah what they hate ˹for themselves˺, and their tongues utter the lie that they will have the finest reward. Without a doubt, for them is the Fire, where they will be abandoned.

q: By Allaah! We have definitely sent Ambiyaa to the nations before you
but Shaytaan beautified their actions for them
(made their evil actions appealing to them so that they reject the message of the Ambiyaa ﵊ who told them to forsake these actions).
shall take charge of their affairs today
and they will have a painful punishment
v.s: By God, We did certainly send [messengers] to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds attractive to them. And he is their [i.e., the disbelievers] ally today [as well], and they will have a painful punishment.
v.c: By Allah! We have surely sent messengers to communities before you ˹O Prophet˺, but Satan made their misdeeds appealing to them. So he is their patron today, and they will suffer a painful punishment.

q: as guidance and a mercy for the Mu'mineen.
v.s: And We have not revealed to you the Book, [O Muhammad], except for you to make clear to them that wherein they have differed and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
v.c: We have revealed to you the Book only to clarify for them what they differed about, and as a guide and mercy for those who believe.

q: Allaah sends rain from the sky, by which He revives the earth after its death
(after it has become dry and empty).
There is certainly an Aayah in this
v.s: And God has sent down rain from the sky and given life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen.
v.c: And Allah sends down rain from the sky, giving life to the earth after its death. Surely in this is a sign for those who listen.

q: There is certainly a lesson for you in livestock
(signs that point towards Allaah's greatness and Towheed).
From what is in their bellies between excrement
and blood, We give you pure milk to drink that is easily consumed.
(Although the stomach of animals is an impure environment having blood and excreta always present, Allaah has the immense power to create pure and palatable milk there.)
v.s: And indeed, for you in grazing livestock is a lesson. We give you drink from what is in their bellies - between excretion and blood - pure milk, palatable to drinkers.
v.c: And there is certainly a lesson for you in cattle: We give you to drink of what is in their bellies, from between digested food and blood: pure milk, pleasant to drink.

q: From the fruits of the date palm
in this for those who understand
(those who understand that Allaah's bounties like grapes should not be used to make Haraam things like wine).
v.s: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason.
v.c: And from the fruits of palm trees and grapevines you derive intoxicants as well as wholesome provision. Surely in this is a sign for those who understand.

q: in the mountains, in the trees and in the buildings they
v.s: And your Lord inspired to the bee, "Take for yourself among the mountains, houses [i.e., hives], and among the trees and [in] that which they construct.
v.c: And your Lord inspired the bees: “Make ˹your˺ homes in the mountains, the trees, and in what people construct,

q: “...Then eat from every type of fruit
and travel through the pathways of your Rabb

(for you to travel on. Allaah has created pathways in the air for bees to fly in on so that they can always find their way back to their own hives regardless of how far they travel to gather nectar).”
(sometimes dark in colour, sometimes light changing according to season and the age of the bee)
emerges from its belly, in which lies a cure for man
Indeed in this is an Aayah
v.s: Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord laid down [for you]." There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought.
v.c: and feed from ˹the flower of˺ any fruit ˹you please˺ and follow the ways your Lord has made easy for you.” From their bellies comes forth liquid of varying colours, in which there is healing for people. Surely in this is a sign for those who reflect.

q: Allaah created you and will then claim your souls
(when the time for your death arrives).
There are those of you who will be returned to a worthless
so that he knows nothing after once possessing
knowledge. Undoubtedly Allaah is All Knowing, All Powerful.
(According to the Ahadeeth, those who learn and teach the Ahadeeth as well as those who regularly recite the Qur'aan will, Insha Allaah, not suffer from senility.)
v.s: And God created you; then He will take you in death. And among you is he who is reversed to the most decrepit [old] age so that he will not know, after [having had] knowledge, a thing. Indeed, God is Knowing and Competent.
v.c: Allah has created you, and then causes you to die. And some of you are left to reach the most feeble stage of life so that they may know nothing after having known much. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing, Most Capable.

q: Allaah has given some of you preference over others in sustenance
(Allaah has given some people more wealth and provisions than others. Therefore, none should feel proud about what he has been given just as none should be jealous of what has been given to others).
Now those who have been granted preference
to their slaves so as to make them all equal.

(Masters and slaves are not equal in terms of material wealth because the slave and all his possessions actually belong to the master. In a like manner, Allaah's creation cannot be equal to Him because He owns them and whatever they have. It is therefore foolish to attribute partners to Him. Despite understanding this example,)
(by worshipping others instead of Him when He has given them all they have)?
v.s: And God has favored some of you over others in provision. But those who were favored [i.e., given more] would not hand over their provision to those whom their right hands possess [i.e., slaves] so they would be equal to them therein. Then is it the favor of God they reject?
v.c: And Allah has favoured some of you over others in provision. But those who have been much favoured would not share their wealth with those ˹bondspeople˺ in their possession, making them their equals. Do they then deny Allah’s favours?

q: Allaah has made spouses for you from yourselves
(from the human race for humans and from the Jinn for the Jinn)
He has provided for you pure foods
(Although they ought to worship Allaah to thank Him for everything He has given them, they foolishly worship other gods that do not give them anything.)
v.s: And God has made for you from yourselves mates and has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren and has provided for you from the good things. Then in falsehood do they believe and in the favor of God they disbelieve?
v.c: And Allah has made for you spouses of your own kind, and given you through your spouses children and grandchildren. And He has granted you good, lawful provisions. Are they then faithful to falsehood and ungrateful for Allah’s favours?

q: worship besides Allaah things that have no control over
any sustenance for them from the skies
(they cannot make anything grow from the soil)
(to provide anything even though they may try everything in their power).
v.s: And they worship besides God that which does not possess for them [the power of] provision from the heavens and the earth at all, and [in fact], they are unable.
v.c: Yet they worship besides Allah those ˹idols˺ who do not afford them any provision from the heavens and the earth, nor do they have the power to.
v.h: Parables for Powerless Gods and Almighty Allah

q: (by saying that certain idols or others have powers similar to Allaah).
Allaah knows and you do not know
v.s: So do not assert similarities to God. Indeed, God knows and you do not know.
v.c: So do not set up equals to Allah, for Allah certainly knows and you do not know.

q: a slave in bondage who has no power to do anything
(because everything has to be done with the permission of his master).
whom Allaah has granted a good provision and he spends from it secretly and openly

(as he pleases without needing permission from anyone. The slave symbolises the gods that the Mushrikeen worship, who have no power to do anything without Allaah's will. Allaah's example is like the second person because He is at liberty to do as He pleases).
(because He deserves all types of praise),
v.s: God presents an example: a slave [who is] owned and unable to do a thing and he to whom We have provided from Us good provision, so he spends from it secretly and publicly. Can they be equal? Praise to God! But most of them do not know.
v.c: Allah sets forth a parable: a slave who lacks all means, compared to a ˹free˺ man to whom We granted a good provision, of which he donates ˹freely,˺ openly and secretly. Are they equal? Praise be to Allah. In fact, most of them do not know.

q: (because he can neither understand anything nor be made to understand anything)
a burden to his guardian. Wherever he is sent
he does not bring any good
(results. In fact, he causes more harm. This is the example of a Kaafir).
Can he be equal to the one who
enjoins justice and is on the straight path
(on Islaam)? (The two can never be equal just as the gods of the Kuffaar cannot be equal to Allaah.)
v.s: And God presents an example of two men, one of them dumb and unable to do a thing, while he is a burden to his guardian. Wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice, while he is on a straight path?
v.c: And Allah sets forth a parable of two men: one of them is dumb, incapable of anything. He is a burden on his master. Wherever he is sent, he brings no good. Can such a person be equal to the one who commands justice and is on the Straight Path?

q: To Allaah belongs the unseen affairs of the heavens and the earth
(Only He has knowledge of everything unseen).
(together with resurrecting all of creation is regarded as an awesome event, yet it is so easy for Allaah that it)
is just like the blink of an eye or even quicker
(because all Allaah does to bring something into being is to say, “Be!” In fact, Allaah does not even have to say this). (This is nothing strange because)
Verily Allaah has power over all things.
v.s: And to God belongs the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. And the command for the Hour is not but as a glance of the eye or even nearer. Indeed, God is over all things competent.
v.c: To Allah ˹alone˺ belongs ˹the knowledge of˺ the unseen in the heavens and the earth. Bringing about the Hour would only take the blink of an eye, or even less. Surely Allah is Most Capable of everything.

q: Allaah removed you from the wombs of your mothers when you knew nothing
blessed you with ears, eyes and hearts so that you may be grateful
(to Him and fulfil all His commands).’
v.s: And God has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers not knowing a thing, and He made for you hearing and vision and hearts [i.e., intellect] that perhaps you would be grateful.
v.c: And Allah brought you out of the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing, and gave you hearing, sight, and intellect so perhaps you would be thankful.

q: Have they not seen the birds subjugated
in mid-air? Only Allaah suspends them in the air
(without Whom, they would fall to the ground like all other creatures).
Indeed there are Aayaat in this for the people who have Imaan.
v.s: Do they not see the birds controlled in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them up except God. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
v.c: Have they not seen the birds glide in the open sky? None holds them up except Allah. Surely in this are signs for those who believe.

q: And Allaah has granted you an abode
(a place to rest and to live)
in your homes and made homes
for you from the hides of animals, which you find light
when you travel and when you pitch camp
from their wool, their fur and their hair
(for as long as you live or as long as they last).
v.s: And God has made for you from your homes a place of rest and made for you from the hides of the animals tents which you find light on your day of travel and your day of encampment; and from their wool, fur and hair is furnishing and enjoyment [i.e., provision] for a time.
v.c: And Allah has made your homes a place to rest, and has given you tents from the hide of animals, light to handle when you travel and when you camp. And out of their wool, fur, and hair He has given you furnishings and goods for a while.

q: (Further enumerating the many favours He has blessed man with, Allaah says,)
things that Allaah has created, He has
made those things that provide shade
He has also made for you places of safety in the mountains
and made coats for you that protect you from the heat and coats
(Allaah made the raw materials necessary for these things and it was He who inspired man to make them).
(as He has blessed you with all these favours)
(to Him and fulfil all His commands).
v.s: And God has made for you, from that which He has created, shadows [i.e., shade] and has made for you from the mountains, shelters and has made for you garments which protect you from the heat and garments [i.e., coats of mail] which protect you from your [enemy in] battle. Thus does He complete His favor upon you that you might submit [to Him].
v.c: And Allah has provided you shade out of what He created, and has given you shelter in the mountains. He has also provided you with clothes protecting you from the heat ˹and cold˺, and armour shielding you in battle. This is how He perfects His favour upon you, so perhaps you will ˹fully˺ submit ˹to Him˺.

q: (O Muhammad ﷺ do not worry because)
your only responsibility is clear propagation
(to give them the message clearly after which you cannot force them to accept).
v.s: But if they turn away, [O Muhammad] - then only upon you is [responsibility for] clear notification.
v.c: But if they turn away, then your duty ˹O Prophet˺ is only to deliver ˹the message˺ clearly.

q: (by worshipping other gods as if those gods had given them what they have). (This behaviour makes it apparent that)
v.s: They recognize the favor of God; then they deny it. And most of them are disbelievers.
v.c: They are aware of Allah’s favours, but still deny them. And most of them are ˹truly˺ ungrateful.

m: will be asked to make amends
q: when We shall raise a witness
(who will testify about the behaviour of his nation),
then the Kuffaar will not be granted permission
nor will they be allowed to please Allaah
(by repenting or doing something good to make amends because it will then be too late. The time for making amends and seeking forgiveness is restricted to this world).
v.s: And [mention] the Day when We will resurrect from every nation a witness [i.e., their prophet]. Then it will not be permitted to the disbelievers [to apologize or make excuses], nor will they be asked to appease [God].
v.c: ˹Consider, O Prophet,˺ the Day We will call ˹a prophet as˺ a witness from every faith-community. Then the disbelievers will neither be allowed to plead nor appease ˹their Lord˺.

q: (of Jahannam and are made to enter it,)
for them, nor will they be granted reprieve
(no bail will be accepted nor will any leniency be shown then).
v.s: And when those who wronged see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
v.c: And when the wrongdoers face the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be delayed ˹from it˺.

q: When the Mushrikeen will see their partners
(the idols and gods they regarded as Allaah's partners),
they will exclaim, “O our Rabb! These are our partners that we used to worship instead of You.” Then the word will be flung back to them
(when these gods will deny that they were worshipped and say):

(Idols will deny being worshipped because being lifeless, they had no idea that they were worshipped. As for living beings who were regarded as gods, they will deny being worshipped because the object of worship is to please the one being worshipped and instead of pleasing the ones being worshipped, the worshippers will have caused more problems for them, especially in the Aakhirah. Therefore, since) the object of worship is lost, it is as if no worship took place at all. See also verse 28 of Surah 10 and verse 82 of Surah 19.)
v.s: And when those who associated others with God see their “partners,” they will say, “Our Lord, these are our partners [to You] whom we used to invoke besides You.” But they will throw at them the statement, “Indeed, you are liars.”
v.c: And when the polytheists see their associate-gods, they will say, “Our Lord! These are our associate-gods that we used to invoke besides You.” Their gods will throw a rebuttal at them, ˹saying,˺ “You are definitely liars.”

q: will offer their submission to Allaah on that day
they used to fabricate will be lost to them
(their gods will be unable to intercede on their behalf as they had anticipated in this world).
v.s: And they will impart to God that Day [their] submission, and lost from them is what they used to invent.
v.c: They will offer ˹full˺ submission to Allah on that Day, and whatever ˹gods˺ they fabricated will fail them.

q: For those who commit kufr and who prevent
from Allaah's path, We shall add punishment to their punishment because of the corruption that they caused
(together with suffering for their own wrongdoing, they will also suffer for the wrongdoing of those whom they encouraged to do wrong).
v.s: Those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of God - We will increase them in punishment over [their] punishment for what corruption they were causing.
v.c: For those who disbelieve and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, We will add more punishment to their punishment for all the corruption they spread.

q: The day when We shall raise against every nation a witness from their midst
(the Ambiyaa ﵊ of every nation who will testify against the Kuffaar of their nations),
(to testify in favour of the Ambiyaa ﵊ that they did fulfil their responsibilities).
to you that explains all things to you
(including the fact that all the Ambiyaa ﵊) their duties)
guidance, a mercy and good news
v.s: And [mention] the Day when We will resurrect among every nation a witness over them from themselves [i.e., their prophet]. And We will bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these [i.e., your nation]. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.
v.c: ˹Consider, O Prophet,˺ the Day We will call against every faith-community a witness of their own. And We will call you to be a witness against these ˹people of yours˺. We have revealed to you the Book as an explanation of all things, a guide, a mercy, and good news for those who ˹fully˺ submit.

q: (to do everything to the best of ones ability and to do everything with the consciousness that Allaah is watching),
to relatives. And Allaah forbids immoral behaviour, evil and oppression. He advises you so that you may take heed
(and thereby save ourselves from ruin and Jahannam).
v.s: Indeed, God orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that perhaps you will be reminded.
v.c: Indeed, Allah commands justice, grace, as well as courtesy to close relatives. He forbids indecency, wickedness, and aggression. He instructs you so perhaps you will be mindful.

q: (the Pledge of Alist and all pledges with people that Allaah requires you to fulfil)
once you make the pledge. Do not break your vows
when you have already made Allaah a Witness upon yourselves
(by swearing the oaths in His name).
Indeed Allaah knows what you do
v.s: And fulfill the covenant of God when you have taken it, [O believers], and do not break oaths after their confirmation while you have made God, over you, a security [i.e., witness]. Indeed, God knows what you do.
v.c: Honour Allah’s covenant when you make a pledge, and do not break your oaths after confirming them, having made Allah your guarantor. Surely Allah knows all you do.

q: like the woman who shredded her spun yarn to threads after strengthening it

(she shredded it after all her effort of spinning it. Just as this verse refers to breaking vows after solemnising them, it also refers to abandoning an act like salaah or Hajj without completing it). (Referring to the practice of certain Arab tribes who used to break the treaties they had made with small tribes so that they could enter into treaties with larger tribes, Allaah says,)
a means of causing corruption between you because a nation is larger in number than another. The fact of the matter is that Allaah only tests you by it
(by these vows to see who will abide by them and who will not).
And, on the Day of Judgement, He will certainly make clear to you the matters about which you differed
(and then the sinners will be punished for their sins).
v.s: And do not be like she who untwisted her spun thread after it was strong [by] taking your oaths as [means of] deceit between you because one community is more plentiful [in number or wealth] than another community. God only tries you thereby. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ.
v.c: Do not be like the woman who ˹foolishly˺ unravels her yarn after it is firmly spun, by taking your oaths as a means of deceiving one another in favour of a stronger group. Surely Allah tests you through this. And on the Day of Judgment He will certainly make your differences clear to you.

m: And surely you will be questioned
q: If Allaah willed, He would have made you a single nation but He sends astray whoever He wills and guides whoever He wills

(for reasons that conform with His perfect wisdom and knowledge). (Whereas those gone astray do not always suffer punishment in this world, they should not think that they will escape punishment in the Aakhirah as well because then)
You will definitely be questioned about what
(and you will be punished for the wrong you did).
v.s: And if God had willed, He could have made you [of] one religion, but He causes to stray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
v.c: Had Allah willed, He could have easily made you one community ˹of believers˺, but He leaves to stray whoever He wills and guides whoever He wills. And you will certainly be questioned about what you used to do.

q: (Warning Muslims that they should not take oaths with the intention of breaking them because this will cause others to do the same even though they had not intended to do so, Allaah says,)
Do not make your oaths a means of causing corruption between you
(causing others to break their oaths like you),
so as to make a foot slip
(when they had not intended to do so),
and so as to make you taste the punishment of preventing
Yours shall be an intense punishment
v.s: And do not take your oaths as [means of] deceit between you, lest a foot slip after it was [once] firm, and you would taste evil [in this world] for what [people] you diverted from the way of God, and you would have [in the Hereafter] a great punishment.
v.c: And do not take your oaths as a means of deceiving one another or your feet will slip after they have been firm. Then you will taste the evil ˹consequences˺ of hindering ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah, and you will suffer a tremendous punishment.

q: Do not purchase a small sum
(the Pledge of Alist and all pledges with all others that Allaah requires you to fulfil).
is better for you if you but knew
v.s: And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price. Indeed, what is with God is best for you, if only you could know.
v.c: And do not trade Allah’s covenant for a fleeting gain. What is with Allah is certainly far better for you, if only you knew.

q: shall come to an end and what is with Allaah
will last forever. We shall most definitely reward those who are exercise sabr
for the good deeds that they do.
v.s: Whatever you have will end, but what God has is lasting. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.
v.c: Whatever you have will end, but whatever Allah has is everlasting. And We will certainly reward the steadfast according to the best of their deeds.

m: then surely We will give him life
q: As for that male or female who does good and is a Mu'min, We will certainly grant them a good
for the good that they do.
v.s: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely give them their reward [in the Hereafter] according to the best of what they used to do.
v.c: Whoever does good, whether male or female, and is a believer, We will surely bless them with a good life, and We will certainly reward them according to the best of their deeds.

q: When you recite the Qur'aan, then
seek Allaah's protection from the accursed Shaytaan
(by reciting “A Oodhu Billaahi Minash Shaytaanir Rajeem” before commencing the recital).
v.s: So when you recite the Qur’ān, [first] seek refuge in God from Satan, the expelled [from His mercy].
v.c: When you recite the Quran, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the accursed.

q: has no control over those who have Imaan and who rely solely on their Rabb
v.s: Indeed, there is for him no authority over those who have believed and rely upon their Lord.
v.c: He certainly has no authority over those who believe and put their trust in their Lord.

q: His control is only over those who befriend him
v.s: His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who through him associate others with God.
v.c: His authority is only over those who take him as a patron and who—under his influence—associate ˹others˺ with Allah ˹in worship˺.

q: and Allaah knows best what He reveals
However, most of them have no knowledge
(they do not know that Allaah replaces commands with only what is better for people).
v.s: And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse - and God is most knowing of what He sends down - they say, “You, [O Muhammad], are but an inventor [of lies].” But most of them do not know.
v.c: When We replace a verse with another—and Allah knows best what He reveals—they say, “You ˹Muḥammad˺ are just a fabricator.” In fact, most of them do not know.

q: Say, “The Ruhul Qudus has revealed it with truth from your Rabb to make the Mu'mineen steadfast
guidance and good news for the Muslims.”
v.s: Say, [O Muhammad], “The Pure Spirit [i.e., Gabriel] has brought it down from your Lord in truth to make firm those who believe and as guidance and good tidings to the Muslims.”
v.c: Say, “The holy spirit has brought it down from your Lord with the truth to reassure the believers, and as a guide and good news for those who submit ˹to Allah˺.”

q: Indeed We know well that they
The language of the person to whom they refer is Ajami
is in the clear Arabic language
(How is it possible for a person whose language is not Arabic to speak such Arabic that even the most eloquent Arabs are unable to match it?).
v.s: And We certainly know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him [i.e., the Prophet (ﷺ)]." The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, and this [recitation, i.e., Qur’ān] is [in] a clear Arabic language.
v.c: And We surely know that they say, “No one is teaching him except a human.” But the man they refer to speaks a foreign tongue, whereas this ˹Quran˺ is ˹in˺ eloquent Arabic.

q: Verily Allaah will not guide those who do not believe in His Aayaat
(because they do not want to be guided).
v.s: Indeed, those who do not believe in the verses of God - God will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
v.c: Surely those who do not believe in Allah’s revelations will never be guided by Allah, and they will suffer a painful punishment.

q: Those who do not believe in Allaah's Aayaat merely invent lies
(about the Qur'aan by saying that it is not from Allaah and they lie about Allaah by saying that He has partners).
(and not those like Rasulullaah ﷺ whom they label as liars)!
v.s: They only invent falsehood who do not believe in the verses of God, and it is those who are the liars.
v.c: No one fabricates lies except those who disbelieve in Allah’s revelations, and it is they who are the ˹true˺ liars.

q: Except for the person who is forced
(to make statements of kufr for fear of losing his life)
content with Imaan, those who disbelieve in Allaah after having Imaan and who open their hearts to kufr
will have Allaah's wrath on them and they shall suffer a terrible punishment.
v.s: Whoever disbelieves in [i.e., denies] God after his belief... except for one who is forced [to renounce his religion] while his heart is secure in faith. But those who [willingly] open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from God, and for them is a great punishment;
v.c: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after their belief—not those who are forced while their hearts are firm in faith, but those who embrace disbelief wholeheartedly—they will be condemned by Allah and suffer a tremendous punishment.

q: is because they prefer the life of this world to the Aakhirah. Allaah certainly does not guide those who commit kufr
v.s: That is because they preferred the worldly life over the Hereafter and that God does not guide the disbelieving people.
v.c: This is because they prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter. Surely Allah never guides those who ˹choose to˺ disbelieve.

q: These are the ones on whose hearts, ears and eyes Allaah has set a seal
(which prevents them from understanding, hearing and seeing the truth).
v.s: Those are the ones over whose hearts and hearing and vision God has sealed, and it is those who are the heedless.
v.c: They are the ones whose hearts, ears, and eyes are sealed by Allah, and it is they who are ˹truly˺ heedless.

q: Without doubt, they will be the losers in the Aakhirah.
v.s: Assuredly, it is they, in the Hereafter, who will be the losers.
v.c: Without a doubt, they will be the losers in the Hereafter.

m: they had been put to trials
q: Your Rabb shall be Most Forgiving and Most Merciful after all towards those who make Hijrah after being tried
(after being tortured by the Mushrikeen and forced to make statements of Kufr)
strive in His way and exercise sabr.
v.s: Then, indeed your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been compelled [to renounce their religion] and thereafter fought [for the cause of God] and were patient - indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful
v.c: As for those who emigrated after being compelled ˹to renounce Islam˺, then struggled ˹in Allah’s cause˺, and persevered, your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ is truly All-Forgiving, Most Merciful after all.

m: and will be paid in full
q: when every person shall argue for
and every soul shall be rewarded in full for its actions and they will not be oppressed
(no one will be punished for a sin s/he did not commit nor deprived of any reward that s/he deserves).
v.s: On the Day when every soul will come disputing [i.e., pleading] for itself, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and they will not be wronged [i.e., treated unjustly].
v.c: ˹Consider˺ the Day ˹when˺ every soul will come pleading for itself, and each will be paid in full for what it did, and none will be wronged.

q: Allaah gives the example of a town that was peaceful and tranquil
(the residents experienced no fear and had no reason to be displeased).
Their provision came to them in abundance from every avenue
they were ungrateful for Allaah's bounty so, because of their actions, Allaah caused them to taste the garments of hunger and fear
v.s: And God presents an example: a city [i.e., Makkah] which was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location, but it denied the favors of God. So God made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing.
v.c: And Allah sets forth the example of a society which was safe and at ease, receiving its provision in abundance from all directions. But its people met Allah’s favours with ingratitude, so Allah made them taste the clutches of hunger and fear for their misdeeds.

q: Indeed Rusul came to them from among themselves
but they rejected them, because of which punishment
afflicted them while they remained oppressive
v.s: And there had certainly come to them a Messenger from among themselves, but they denied him; so punishment overtook them while they were wrongdoers.
v.c: A messenger of their own actually did come to them, but they denied him. So the torment overtook them while they persisted in wrongdoing.

q: So eat from the pure and lawful things that Allaah has provided for you
and be grateful for Allaah's bounty if it is only He Whom you worship.
v.s: Then eat of what God has provided for you [which is] lawful and good. And be grateful for the favor of God, if it is [indeed] Him that you worship.
v.c: So eat from the good, lawful things which Allah has provided for you, and be grateful for Allah’s favours, if you ˹truly˺ worship Him ˹alone˺.

q: (an animal which dies a natural death or which is not slaughtered or hunted in accordance with the Shari'ah),
(and all other parts of its body),
those animals that were sacrificed with
the name of another besides Allaah
(such as the name of an idol, Jinn, saint, Prophet, etc).
As for him who is driven by
(to eat these forbidden foods for fear of losing his life),
(he may eat them provided that he eats)
(without eating more than is necessary to keep him alive). (Allaah allows this concession because)
Verily Allaah is the Most Forgiving, the Most Merciful
(and has therefore made the Deen very practical.).
v.s: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than God. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit] - then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.
v.c: He has only forbidden you ˹to eat˺ carrion, blood, swine, and what is slaughtered in the name of any other than Allah. But if someone is compelled by necessity—neither driven by desire nor exceeding immediate need—then surely Allah is All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

q: With regard to the false claims your tongues make
“This is Halaal” and “This is Haraam,” so as to invent lies against Allaah
(by making it seem as if Allaah has made these things Halaal or Haraam).
Indeed those who invent lies against Allaah will never be successful
v.s: And do not say about what your tongues assert of untruth, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent falsehood about God. Indeed, those who invent falsehood about God will not succeed.
v.c: Do not falsely declare with your tongues, “This is lawful, and that is unlawful,” ˹only˺ fabricating lies against Allah. Indeed, those who fabricate lies against Allah will never succeed.

q: (a little enjoyment in this world because regardless of how much they have, it is temporary and will be left behind).
they shall suffer a torturous punishment.
v.s: [It is but] a brief enjoyment, and they will have a painful punishment.
v.c: ˹It is only˺ a brief enjoyment, then they will suffer a painful punishment.

q: We have forbidden for the Jews the things that We have related to you before
We did not oppress them, but they oppressed themselves
(by doing those things that invited Allaah's punishment when they were warned about it).
v.s: And to those who are Jews We have prohibited that which We related to you before. And We did not wrong them [thereby], but they were wronging themselves.
v.c: To the Jews, We have forbidden what We related to you before. We did not wrong them, but it was they who wronged themselves.

q: Verily your Rabb is certainly Most Forgiving and Most Merciful towards those who commit evil out of ignorance
(ignorant of the true consequences of the sin)
v.s: Then, indeed your Lord, to those who have done wrong out of ignorance and then repent after that and correct themselves - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.
v.c: As for those who commit evil ignorantly ˹or recklessly˺, then repent afterwards and mend their ways, then your Lord is surely All-Forgiving, Most Merciful.

q: Ibraheem ﵊ was certainly a great leader, obedient and Haneef
(one inclined towards the truth and averse to all false creeds).
v.s: Indeed, Abraham was a [comprehensive] leader, devoutly obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.
v.c: Indeed, Abraham was a model of excellence: devoted to Allah, ˹perfectly˺ upright—not a polytheist—

q: He was grateful for Allaah's favours. Allaah chose him
(to be a Rasool and a special friend)
and guided him to the straight path.
v.s: [He was] grateful for His favors. He [i.e., God] chose him and guided him to a straight path.
v.c: ˹utterly˺ grateful for Allah’s favours. ˹So˺ He chose him and guided him to the Straight Path.

q: We granted him good in this world
(he is praised and respected by people of all religions)
and he shall be from the righteous in the Aakhirah.
v.s: And We gave him good in this world, and indeed, in the Hereafter he will be among the righteous.
v.c: We blessed him with all goodness in this world, and in the Hereafter he will certainly be among the righteous.

q: Then We sent revelation to you
“Follow the religion of Ibraheem that is Haneef
(inclined towards the truth and averse to all false creeds).
(These words are repeated to emphasise the fact that Ibraheem ﵊ was neither a Jew nor a Christian as the Jews and Christians claimed.)
v.s: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not of those who associate with God.
v.c: Then We revealed to you ˹O Prophet, saying˺: “Follow the faith of Abraham, the upright, who was not one of the polytheists.”

q: (when some of them held the day sacred while others did not).
Undoubtedly your Rabb will decide between them on the Day of Qiyaamah concerning the matters about which they differed.
v.s: The sabbath was only appointed for those who differed over it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
v.c: ˹Honouring˺ the Sabbath was ordained only for those who disputed about Abraham. And surely your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Judgment regarding their disputes.

q: to the path of your Rabb
in a manner that is best
(without driving them further away from Islaam).
Indeed your Rabb knows best who strays from His path and He knows best who are the rightly guided ones
(You have no such knowledge and are therefore bound to call everyone to Islaam).
v.s: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided.
v.c: Invite ˹all˺ to the Way of your Lord with wisdom and kind advice, and only debate with them in the best manner. Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided.

q: then avenge yourself in proportion to the aggression
then this is definitely best for the patient ones
(because this will soften the heart of your opponent and attract him towards you).
v.s: And if you punish [an enemy, O believers], punish with an equivalent of that with which you were harmed. But if you are patient - it is better for those who are patient.
v.c: If you retaliate, then let it be equivalent to what you have suffered. But if you patiently endure, it is certainly best for those who are patient.

q: Be patient! Your patience is only from Allaah
(only Allaah can give you the ability to exercise patience).
(the Kuffaar when they refuse to accept Islaam)
and do not be saddened by their plotting
(against you because Allaah will see to them).
v.s: And be patient, [O Muhammad], and your patience is not but through God. And do not grieve over them and do not be in distress over what they conspire.
v.c: Be patient ˹O Prophet˺, for your patience is only with Allah’s help. Do not grieve over those ˹who disbelieve˺, nor be distressed by their schemes.

q: Undoubtedly Allaah is with those who adopt Taqwa and with those who adopt the path of
(Allaah shall assist them against all their enemies).
v.s: Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good.
v.c: Surely Allah is with those who shun evil and who do good ˹deeds˺.
